title: handle_continue_link doc says ok:false only on Resend failure, but upsert failure also returns ok:false (200, not 500)
detail: The doc comment promises ok:false only when the Resend call fails and 500s for DB failures, yet an upsert DB failure yields ok:false with HTTP 200. Either the comment or the behaviour is wrong.
recommended_fix: Align the two: either return 500 on upsert failure per the doc, or amend the doc to state upsert-failure also answers ok:false/200.

title: strip_draft_on_submit does not clear last_link_sent_at, so submitted drafts keep counting toward the hourly fan-out bound
evidence:
UPDATE application_draft
SET fields = '{}'::jsonb,
    continue_token = NULL,
    submitted_at = now(),
    updated_at = now()
WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  AND email = lower($2)
-- vs claim_continue_link_send.sql:
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d2
    WHERE d2.email = lower($2)
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at IS NOT NULL
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
-- vs erase_draft_by_token.sql which does: last_link_sent_at = NULL,
detail: Erasure clears last_link_sent_at; submit does not. A recently-emailed-then-submitted draft still occupies a slot in the 3-per-hour cross-vacancy count for the same recipient, skewing the bound.
recommended_fix: Add last_link_sent_at = NULL to strip_draft_on_submit's SET clause, matching the erasure tombstone.

title: upsert_application_draft ON CONFLICT does not bump updated_at while strip_draft_on_submit maintains it manually
evidence:
ON CONFLICT (vacancy_id, email) DO UPDATE
  SET fields = EXCLUDED.fields,
      continue_token = COALESCE(
        application_draft.continue_token,
        EXCLUDED.continue_token
      )
-- contrast strip_draft_on_submit.sql:
    submitted_at = now(),
    updated_at = now()
detail: strip_draft_on_submit sets updated_at = now() explicitly, proving the column exists and is maintained by hand. The hot upsert path (every debounced save) never touches it, so updated_at goes stale on the most-updated rows.
recommended_fix: Add updated_at = now() to the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET clause, or document why draft saves must not move updated_at.

title: Draft strip runs before file-resolution work in finalise_application; a later failure leaves the applicant with neither draft nor a perceived-successful submit
detail: The strip is placed ahead of document owner resolution (and presumably uploads). If any later step fails the request, the user sees a failed submission while the saved-draft PII is already wiped and the continue token killed.
recommended_fix: Move the strip to the end of finalise_application (after all fallible steps), or confirm nothing after this point can fail the submission.

title: Send-failure path clears the cooldown stamp, also removing the row from the hourly fan-out count
detail: clear_last_link_sent sets last_link_sent_at = NULL, which both lifts the 10-minute cooldown and drops the row from the 3-per-hour cross-vacancy count. During a Resend outage every retry re-claims and re-clears, so the bounds effectively vanish exactly when sends are failing.
recommended_fix: Acceptable as designed, but consider a separate last_link_attempted_at for the fan-out count so failed sends still rate-limit claim attempts.

title: Save endpoint reports ok:true when the 500-draft per-vacancy cap silently discards the upsert
evidence:
OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
ON CONFLICT (vacancy_id, email) DO UPDATE
-- handler:
                    Ok(_) -> {
...
                      wisp.json_response(json_ok(True), 200)
detail: When the cap is hit and no (vacancy,email) row exists, INSERT...SELECT inserts nothing and RETURNING yields zero rows; the handler matches Ok(_) and answers ok:true. The applicant's answers are not saved while the UI claims they are.
recommended_fix: Match on the returned row count: Ok(pog.Returned(_, [])) after a non-empty upsert should log and return a distinct response (e.g. ok:false) instead of ok:true.

title: Five form_copy constants have no Gleam reference anywhere in the diff (only consumed by form_draft.js)
evidence:
pub const draft_prep_note: String = ...
pub const draft_continue_button: String = "Email me a link to continue"
pub const draft_continue_sent: String = ...
pub const draft_continue_needs_email: String = ...
pub const draft_continue_failed: String = ...
-- header comment: 'The prep-note swap and the continue-link button strings ALSO live in `priv/static/form_draft.js` (plain static JS can't import Gleam) — KEEP IN SYNC'
detail: draft_prep_note, draft_continue_button, draft_continue_sent, draft_continue_needs_email and draft_continue_failed are defined in Gleam but only the static JS uses these strings; nothing server-side renders them. They exist solely as a sync-prone duplicate source of truth.
recommended_fix: Either reference them server-side (e.g. inject into the page for JS to read) or drop the Gleam copies and keep a single canonical home in form_draft.js.

title: Redundant COALESCE on continue_token in two queries whose own clauses guarantee non-NULL
evidence:
RETURNING COALESCE(continue_token, '') AS continue_token;
-- same statement already ran: SET continue_token = COALESCE(continue_token, $3)
-- and in list_resumable_draft_tokens.sql:
SELECT email, COALESCE(continue_token, '') AS continue_token
FROM application_draft
WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  AND submitted_at IS NULL
  AND continue_token IS NOT NULL;
detail: In claim_continue_link_send the SET clause makes continue_token non-NULL before RETURNING is evaluated; in list_resumable_draft_tokens the WHERE continue_token IS NOT NULL does the same. Both COALESCEs are dead and mask future regressions.
recommended_fix: Return continue_token directly in both queries; the guarantees are already enforced by the SET/WHERE clauses.
